meta.name: RMM Persistence, Evasion, and Secondary Payloads
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has established persistent access using a legitimate RMM tool configured as a service, potentially using renamed binaries or DLL sideloading to evade standard process monitoring, and is using it to deploy secondary infostealers.

references.name: Red Canary — The dual-use dilemma: Rethinking detection for remote access tool abuse

hunt.name: RMM Persistence, Evasion, and Secondary Payloads
hunt.description: Threat actors are increasingly abusing legitimate Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools like NetSupport, ITarian, and RemotePC. These tools provide signed binaries that bypass reputation checks. This hunt identifies persistence through service registry keys, detects evasion through metadata-to-filename mismatches (renamed RMMs), hunts for DLL sideloading indicators in ITarian environments, and looks for secondary payloads like DICOMportable or DeerStealer.

series.title: The dual-use dilemma: Rethinking detection for remote access tool abuse

config.rationale: An adversary has established persistent access using a legitimate RMM tool configured as a service, potentially using renamed binaries or DLL sideloading to evade standard process monitoring, and is using it to deploy secondary infostealers.
blind_spots: RMM tools that run entirely in memory or via PowerShell without dropping a binary (though secondary scripts would still be visible).
Legitimate IT tools that are renamed by admins for internal convenience (high false positive risk).
Hosts without hb_module_activity enabled will miss the sideloading checks.
config.scoping_notes: Focus on endpoints with high user activity first, as phishing is the primary entry vector. Prioritize servers where 'Program Files' exclusions might exist for IT tools.
config.beyond_detection: A single rule might flag 'NetSupport', but it won't distinguish between an IT-sanctioned deployment and a renamed 'Ecard9140.exe' binary that sideloads HijackLoader. This hunt pivots from registry services to process metadata to module loads, building a context of abuse that a reputation-based alert would miss.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(reg_value_data) AS service_path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count FROM hb_registry_activity WHERE LOWER(reg_target) LIKE '%\system\currentcontrolset\services\%\imagepath' AND (LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%client32.exe%' OR LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%hostservice.exe%' OR LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%\users\public\%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY service_path HAVING host_count <= 5 ORDER BY host_count ASC
config.description: Identify RMM-related services running from non-standard locations (like C:\Users\Public) or identified as known abused tools.
config.expected_signal: A list of service paths found on only a few machines; legitimately managed RMMs should appear fleet-wide, while malicious instances will be rare.

primitive_config.label: Stack-count rare RMM service paths
primitive_config.content: SELECT LOWER(reg_value_data) AS service_path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count FROM hb_registry_activity WHERE LOWER(reg_target) LIKE '%\system\currentcontrolset\services\%\imagepath' AND (LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%client32.exe%' OR LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%hostservice.exe%' OR LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%\users\public\%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY service_path HAVING host_count <= 5 ORDER BY host_count ASC

nodes.label: Detect renamed RMM binaries via metadata

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_file_description, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_file_description) LIKE '%simplehelp%' OR LOWER(process_file_description) LIKE '%remotepc%' OR LOWER(process_file_description) LIKE '%netsupport%' OR LOWER(process_file_description) LIKE '%screenconnect%') AND (LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%simplehelp%' AND LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%remotepc%' AND LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%client32%' AND LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%screenconnect%' AND LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%installer%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify binaries that have been renamed to deceptive titles (like 'Ecard' or 'Statement') but retain RMM-related internal metadata.
config.expected_signal: Processes where the description identifies them as RMM software but the binary filename is deceptive. This indicates manual evasion.

primitive_config.label: Detect renamed RMM binaries via metadata
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_file_description, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_file_description) LIKE '%simplehelp%' OR LOWER(process_file_description) LIKE '%remotepc%' OR LOWER(process_file_description) LIKE '%netsupport%' OR LOWER(process_file_description) LIKE '%screenconnect%') AND (LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%simplehelp%' AND LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%remotepc%' AND LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%client32%' AND LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%screenconnect%' AND LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%installer%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')

nodes.label: Hunt for DLL sideloading in RMM processes

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, module_name, module_path, time FROM hb_module_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%rmmservice.exe%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%dicomportable.exe%') AND LOWER(module_path) NOT LIKE 'c:\windows\%' AND LOWER(module_path) NOT LIKE 'c:\program files\%' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Look for non-system DLLs loaded by RMM processes like ITarian's RMMService.exe, which is a known technique for HijackLoader.
config.expected_signal: A list of non-standard modules loaded by RMM binaries from writable or unusual paths, suggesting DLL sideloading.

primitive_config.label: Hunt for DLL sideloading in RMM processes
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, module_name, module_path, time FROM hb_module_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%rmmservice.exe%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%dicomportable.exe%') AND LOWER(module_path) NOT LIKE 'c:\windows\%' AND LOWER(module_path) NOT LIKE 'c:\program files\%' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, file_name, actor_user_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (LOWER(file_name) LIKE '{{rmm_file_names}}' OR LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%dicomportable.zip%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\pdqconnectagent\token%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find specific configuration files and secondary ZIP payloads associated with recent RMM-based ransomware precursor campaigns.
config.expected_signal: File events for .ini configuration files, PDQ token files in ProgramData, or the DICOMportable ZIP file, which often precedes infostealer execution.

primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, file_name, actor_user_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (LOWER(file_name) LIKE '{{rmm_file_names}}' OR LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%dicomportable.zip%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\pdqconnectagent\token%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')

config.objective: Determine if any host has a combination of rare RMM services, renamed RMM binaries, and secondary payload files (DICOMportable/DeerStealer).
config.description: Correlate service creation, renamed binaries, and sideloading activity to determine if the RMM usage is malicious.
config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict identifying whether a specific RMM instance is an adversary loader or a legitimate IT tool.
config.success_criteria: Citations of specific rows in context that show a correlation between an RMM tool and suspicious file/module activity.

config.question: the triage verdict is malicious or suspicious for at least one host
config.condition: the triage verdict is malicious or suspicious for at least one host
config.description: Route the hunt based on the agent's findings.
Prevent further C2 or data exfiltration by isolating the host.
config.instructions: Isolate the endpoint and initiate a full forensic capture of the RMM working directory and configuration files.

config.description: Final human review of the triage and potential isolation.
config.instructions: Review the correlated events from the triage agent. Check if the RMM is part of a legitimate IT project or if the 'renamed' binaries are part of a known phishing lure.

config.description: Finalize the hunt when no malicious activity is found.
config.instructions: No significant anomalies were found. Document that no rare/renamed RMM binaries were detected in the specified lookback window.
